# Ezra Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 470v–471r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down in front of the temple, a huge crowd of Israelites — men, women, and children — gathered around him. The people were weeping bitterly.

**2** Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, from the family of Elam, spoke up: "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the peoples around us. But in spite of this, there is still hope for Israel.

**3** Let us now make a covenant with our God to send away all these women and their children. We will follow the advice of my lord Ezra and of all who respect our God's commands. Let it be done according to the Law. **4** Get up, Ezra, for this is your responsibility. We will support you, so take courage and act!"

**5** So Ezra stood and made the leading priests, Levites, and all the people of Israel take a solemn oath to do what Shecaniah had proposed. And they all took the oath.

**6** Then Ezra left the area in front of the temple and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He spent the night there, and he refused to eat or drink because he was still grieving over the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles.

**7** A proclamation was then sent throughout Judah and Jerusalem, ordering all the returned exiles to assemble in Jerusalem. **8** Anyone who failed to appear within three days would, by decision of the leaders and elders, have all his property confiscated and be expelled from the community of returned exiles.

**9** Within three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin had gathered in Jerusalem. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month. Everyone sat in the open square in front of the temple, trembling with distress over the situation — and shivering from the heavy rain.

**10** Then Ezra the priest stood and addressed them: "You have been unfaithful. You have married foreign women, adding to Israel's guilt. **11** Now confess your sin to the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and do what he demands. Separate yourselves from the surrounding peoples and from your foreign wives."

**12** The entire assembly shouted in response, "Yes, you are right! We must do as you say! **13** But there are many of us, and it is the rainy season. We cannot stay out here in the open. Besides, this problem cannot be resolved in a day or two — there are so many of us who have sinned in this way. **14** Let our leaders act on behalf of the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at an appointed time, accompanied by the elders and judges of their town. Let us deal with this systematically until God's burning anger over this matter has been turned away from us."

**15** Only four men opposed this plan: Jonathan son of Asahel, Jahzeiah son of Tikvah, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite, who supported them.

**16** So the returned exiles followed through. Ezra the priest appointed leaders from each family group, all designated by name. They began their investigation on the first day of the tenth month, **17** and by the first day of the first month, three months later, they had reviewed every case of a man married to a foreign woman.

**18** Among the priests, these were found to have married foreign women:

From the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah. **19** They pledged to send away their wives and offered a ram as a guilt offering.

**20** From the family of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah. **21** From Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah. **22** From Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.

**23** Among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also called Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

**24** Among the musicians: Eliashib. Among the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.

**25** Among the rest of the Israelites: From Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah. **26** From Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah. **27** From Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza. **28** From Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai. **29** From Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeramoth. **30** From Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh. **31** From Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, **32** Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah. **33** From Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei. **34** From Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel, **35** Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi, **36** Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, **37** Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu, **38** Bani, Binnui, Shimei, **39** Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, **40** Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai, **41** Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, **42** Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.

**43** From Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.

**44** All of these men had married foreign women, and some of these women had borne children.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — Collective weeping:** The scene is overwhelming — not just Ezra weeping alone, but a vast assembly, including women and children, weeping together. Public, communal grief over corporate sin is rare in any culture, ancient or modern. This is a community facing the consequences of its choices and mourning what it is about to lose.

**Verses 3, 44 — The unspoken tragedy:** The text records the decision to "put away" foreign wives and their children, but it never describes the actual separations. We are told what was decided but not what it looked like when families were torn apart. This silence may be the most theologically significant feature of the chapter. The author does not celebrate the purge, does not describe the women leaving, does not tell us where they went. The silence is deafening — and perhaps deliberate.

**Verse 15 — Recorded dissent:** Four men opposed the plan, and their names are permanently recorded in Scripture. The text does not condemn them or explain their reasoning. Their presence in the record is a reminder that this decision was not unanimous, and that faithful people could look at the same crisis and reach different conclusions.

*— PNEUMA*
